scheme_name: Subsidy Scheme On Establishment Of - 25 Kadaknath/R.I.R. Birds Unit To Scheduled Tribes
description:
The Subsidy Scheme on Establishment of 25 Kadaknath/R.I.R. Birds Unit to Scheduled Tribes is a targeted initiative by the Government of India aimed at promoting poultry farming among Scheduled Tribes.

This scheme was launched in 2020 as part of the broader efforts to enhance the livelihood opportunities for marginalized communities.

The primary objective of the scheme is to provide financial assistance to Scheduled Tribe families for setting up poultry units.

The scheme aims to empower these communities by providing them with sustainable income sources through poultry farming.

The specific target is to establish 25 Kadaknath or Rhode Island Red birds units for each eligible Scheduled Tribe family.

The scheme is designed to improve the nutritional standards of these communities by promoting the consumption of poultry products.

Each unit will consist of 25 birds which can significantly contribute to the income of the beneficiaries.

The financial assistance provided under this scheme is up to INR 25,000 per unit.

This amount is intended to cover the costs associated with purchasing birds, feed, housing, and other necessary equipment.

The scheme is expected to benefit approximately 10,000 Scheduled Tribe families across various states in India.

The eligibility criteria for this scheme are specifically designed to ensure that only those from Scheduled Tribes can apply.

Applicants must belong to a Scheduled Tribe as recognized by the Government of India.

There is no specific age limit mentioned for applicants.

However, the applicants must have a basic understanding of poultry farming practices.

They should also be willing to undergo training if required.

The application process involves several steps to ensure transparency and accountability.

Interested beneficiaries must first approach the local Animal Husbandry Department.

They need to fill out an application form which can be obtained from the department's office or its official website.

The application form requires details such as the applicant's name, address, tribe, and proposed location for the poultry unit.

Along with the application form, applicants must submit identity proof and caste certificates to verify their Scheduled Tribe status.

Additionally, a project report detailing the proposed poultry unit's setup and operational plan may be required.

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the officials in the Animal Husbandry Department.

The review process typically takes about 15 to 30 days.

If the application is approved, the applicant will receive a sanction order.

The subsidy amount will then be disbursed directly to the beneficiary's bank account.

The disbursement is usually made in one installment after the completion of the unit setup.

Beneficiaries are expected to complete the setup within a stipulated time frame of three months from the date of receiving the sanction order.

The scheme is implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying under the Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying.

The contact details for the Department can be found on the official government website.

The scheme is part of a larger framework of initiatives aimed at improving the socio-economic conditions of Scheduled Tribes in India.

The government has allocated a budget of INR 50 crores for this scheme in the financial year 2021-2022.

This budget is intended to support the establishment of approximately 20,000 poultry units across the country.

The success of the scheme will be monitored through regular assessments and feedback from beneficiaries.

The government aims to achieve a target of at least 60% of the units being operational within the first year of implementation.

Training programs will be organized in collaboration with local agricultural universities and veterinary colleges.

These training programs will cover essential topics such as bird management, feeding practices, disease control, and marketing strategies.

The government is also working on creating a market linkage for the products produced by these poultry units.

This will help ensure that the beneficiaries can sell their products at fair prices.

The scheme is expected to contribute to the overall development of rural areas by creating employment opportunities.

It will also help in reducing poverty levels among Scheduled Tribe communities.

The nutritional benefits of consuming poultry products are significant as they are rich in protein and essential vitamins.

The Kadaknath breed is particularly valued for its black meat which is considered a delicacy and has high market demand.

Rhode Island Red birds are known for their hardiness and good egg-laying capabilities.

The government is also promoting the use of organic farming practices within this scheme.

This aligns with the national goal of promoting sustainable agricultural practices.

The scheme is expected to have a multiplier effect on the local economy by increasing demand for feed and other poultry-related services.

Monitoring and evaluation of the scheme will be conducted through regular field visits and feedback collection from beneficiaries.

The government aims to publish an annual report detailing the progress and impact of the scheme.

This report will include statistics on the number of units established and the income generated by beneficiaries.

The scheme is part of the larger National Livestock Mission which aims to enhance livestock production and productivity.

The government is committed to ensuring that the benefits of this scheme reach the intended beneficiaries without any hindrance.

Awareness campaigns will be conducted to inform potential beneficiaries about the scheme and its benefits.

The overall goal is to create a self-sustaining model of poultry farming among Scheduled Tribes.

This initiative reflects the government's commitment to inclusive growth and development.

The scheme is expected to play a crucial role in bridging the income gap between Scheduled Tribes and other communities.

In conclusion, the Subsidy Scheme on Establishment of 25 Kadaknath/R.I.R. Birds Unit to Scheduled Tribes is a significant step towards empowering marginalized communities through sustainable livelihood opportunities.
